title: Data Preservation in High-Energy Physics
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to preserve and reuse data from high-energy physics experiments after the original collaborations and detector operations have ended. It argues that these datasets are scientifically valuable because they are often unique, costly to reproduce, and potentially useful for new theoretical work, cross-experiment combinations, re-analyses with improved methods, and educational outreach. The document is an intermediate report from an international study group convened in 2008–2009 to examine the state of data preservation in high-energy physics.

The paper does not study an educational intervention or AI-supported science inquiry in K-12. Instead, it lays out preservation models ranging from enhanced documentation only, to simplified data formats, to preserving analysis software, to full preservation of reconstruction and simulation software together with raw/basic data. It also discusses the infrastructure, funding, governance, validation, and archival expertise needed to sustain preserved data over time, including the proposed role of a data archivist and the potential use of virtualisation.

The context is the international high-energy physics community, including large collaborations, computing centres, laboratories, and funding agencies. The paper concludes that urgent action is needed because many experiments are nearing or past their end dates, and that full preservation of analysis capability is recommended when feasible. It proposes a global governance structure, the International Data Preservation Forum, to coordinate policy, standards, and access to preserved data.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a grey-literature/consensus report on data preservation policy in high-energy physics, not an empirical K-12 study. It contains no comparison group, no measured educational outcomes, and no causal identification.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper has no direct impact on K-12 science learning outcomes or AI-supported inquiry. Its relevance is only indirect and institutional, focused on HEP archival governance rather than educational effects.

finding.finding_summary: This is a policy/report-style study on high-energy physics data preservation, not an educational intervention experiment. It argues that long-term preservation can improve future scientific opportunities, reuse, and outreach, but it presents no experimental effect estimates or student-level outcome data.
finding.measure: Policy, governance, and data preservation framework recommendations for HEP institutions
